reason: The health check types table row for Elastic Load Balancing health checks says it checks whether the load balancer reports the instance as healthy and that you must turn it on for your Auto Scaling group.
The quote says that after you turn on these checks, an instance ELB reports Unhealthy is marked Unhealthy on its next periodic health check and replaced.
The quote says an instance no longer in the running state is treated as an immediate failure, immediately marked Unhealthy and replaced.
The quote says health checks use the built-in EC2 status checks and, after a grace period, any optional health checks enabled for the group.

Under How Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling minimizes downtime on the health checks page, the quote states the default of provisioning new instances at the same time existing ones are terminated and the request-acceptance risk.

The quote says an unhealthy InService instance is replaced to maintain desired capacity and the new instance launches using the group's current settings and its associated launch template or launch configuration.
The quote says an instance affected by a scheduled event is considered unhealthy and replaced, and does not start shutting down until the timestamp is reached.
The quote names Spot interruption and manual termination as unexpected terminations after which a replacement is launched to maintain desired capacity.
The table row for VPC Lattice health checks says it checks whether VPC Lattice reports the instance healthy and that you must turn it on for the group; the ELB row says the same.
The quote says that by default EC2 Auto Scaling ignores VPC Lattice health check results and you can optionally turn them on for the group.
Under the AWS Regions heading the quote says target tracking with high-resolution metrics is available in all Regions except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions.
The quotes give a metric period lower than 60 seconds, a lowest supported interval of 10 seconds, and the document history row dated November 22, 2024 for high-resolution metrics.

The quotes say code can poll the lifecycle state from the instance to detect termination, that the autoscaling/target-lifecycle-state item is updated when an instance prepares to transition to a steady state, and that the current state cannot be retrieved from metadata.
The quote says a fully configured instance that passes the EC2 health checks enters InService and is counted against the desired capacity.

The quotes state both branches (retained state with a policy set to retain on TerminateHookAbandon; immediate termination without one) and the document history row for instance lifecycle policies is dated November 20, 2025.
The quotes give the min and max healthy percentage range that limits capacity changes during replacement, the launch-first-then-terminate option, and the document history date November 15, 2023.

The quotes say applications use an IAM role for credentials, and for Auto Scaling instances you choose an instance profile in the launch template or launch configuration that lets EC2 pass the role at launch.
The quote says to replace all instances at once, set a minimum healthy percentage of 0 percent.
The quote says a rollback restores the previous configuration and that automatic rollback happens if the refresh fails or a specified CloudWatch alarm goes into ALARM.
The defaults table row Auto rollback shows Disabled (false) for CLI or SDK and Disabled for the console.
The defaults table row Bake time shows Zero in both columns.
The defaults table row Checkpoint delay shows 1 hour (3600 seconds) for CLI or SDK and 1 hour for the console.

The quotes support that a checkpoint pauses the refresh and that without checkpoints replacements run continuously, but the verify, cancel or roll back part is only in the surrounding context, not in either quote.
The defaults table row Checkpoints shows Disabled (false) for CLI or SDK and Disabled for the console.
The defaults table row CloudWatch alarm shows Disabled (null) for CLI or SDK and Disabled for the console.
Under Maximum healthy percentage the quote says the difference between the minimum and maximum cannot be greater than 100.
The quote says new instances launch first before old ones terminate if the minimum healthy percentage is 100 percent, ensuring desired capacity is maintained at all times.
Under Limitations the quote says the maximum time an instance refresh can continue to actively replace instances is 14 days.
The defaults table row says that with no instance maintenance policy the maximum healthy percentage defaults to 100 percent, in both columns.
The defaults table row says that with no instance maintenance policy the minimum healthy percentage defaults to 90 percent, in both columns.

The two quotes define the minimum healthy percentage as the share of desired capacity kept in service, healthy and ready, and the maximum as the share the group can increase to when replacing instances.
The quote says set both minimum and maximum healthy percentage to 100 percent to replace one instance at a time, which changes the refresh to launch before terminating.

The quote says the health-check case is when the new instances do not pass their health checks; the claim's wording attributes the failing health checks to the instances being replaced. The one-hour retry and failure are supported.

The quote names the rolling strategy as default, terminating and launching in batches while maintaining desired capacity, and the replace root volume strategy as replacing only the root volume without terminating the instance.
The defaults table row Scale-in protected instances shows Wait for CLI or SDK and Ignore for the console.
The quote says a scale-out during a refresh launches instances with the desired configuration and the group settings are updated to it after the refresh succeeds.
The defaults table row Skip matching shows Disabled (false) for CLI or SDK and Enabled for the console.
Under Limitations the quote says skip matching does not check code changes deployed from user data and recommends turning it off when user data pulls new code.
The defaults table row Standby instances shows Wait for CLI or SDK and Ignore for the console.
The quote gives the example that a minimum of 90 percent and a maximum of 100 percent replaces 10 percent of capacity at a time.
